This artwork highlights the 'craquelure,' which consists of an intricate web of fine surface cracks that develop as paint ages over centuries. Inside the wood-paneled office, art professionals utilize a burnished bronze instrument to microscopically examine these specific fractures on the surface of the wooden panel retrieved from a sleek ebony case. Because these thousands of tiny, irregular cracks form over many generations through the expansion and contraction of materials, they represent a physical fingerprint that remains distinct to the authentic work. By comparing these microscopic signatures to authorized historical records, the figures successfully verify the artifact's true provenance.
